title: RaC: Robot Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks by Scaling Recovery and Correction
title_zh: RaC：通过扩展恢复与纠错数据学习长程机器人任务
abstract: Modern robot imitation policies plateau far below perfect execution on contact-rich, deformable-object, and long-horizon tasks even with thousands of expert demonstrations. RaC adds a human-in-the-loop training phase after imitation pre-training. During policy rollouts, operators intervene when failure appears imminent, first rewinding the robot to a familiar in-distribution state and then providing a corrective segment that completes the current sub-task. Training on this composition expands the skill repertoire with retry and adaptation behaviors. Across three real-world bimanual tasks—shirt hanging, airtight container lid sealing, and takeout-box packing—and one simulated assembly task, RaC outperforms prior state of the art using 10 times less data-collection time and samples. The trained policy also exhibits test-time scaling as it performs more recovery maneuvers.

editorial.selection_reason: 通过真人干预明确收集“回退到熟悉状态＋完成当前子任务”的恢复轨迹，证明纠错数据比继续增加干净示范更适合提升长程策略可靠性。

uncertainties: 需要人在环判断何时介入并完成恢复。
